description: Biohacking Village focuses on healthcare cybersecurity, medical device security, patient safety, and open-source biotechnology. Talks examine vulnerabilities in connected clinical systems, molecular tagging, DIY biology, and collaborative disclosure between researchers and medical device manufacturers.

talks.title: Fireside Chat
talks.teaser: FDA Principal Deputy Commissioner Amy Abernethy discusses medical device cybersecurity, big data, and regulatory collaboration.
talks.summary:
Big Data and Patient Rights in Modern Healthcare

The discussion explores how real-world data collection can be balanced with patient rights, data privacy, and clinical research requirements in the digital era.

Cybersecurity Risks in Connected Medical Devices

As medical devices become increasingly networked, addressing software vulnerabilities and enforcing robust security baselines is essential to safeguard patient safety.

FDA Collaboration with Security Researchers

The conversation highlights regulatory initiatives, including the FDA-led Evidence Accelerator, designed to foster productive collaboration between federal regulators and independent security researchers.

talks.title: Porcupine: Rapid Robust Tagging with DNA
talks.teaser: Presents Porcupine, a molecular tagging system that uses synthetic DNA strands and portable nanopore sequencers for rapid physical object tagging.
talks.summary:
Molecular Tagging for Physical Objects

Molecular tagging offers an alternative method for labeling physical assets where conventional barcodes or RFID tags are impractical or easily compromised.

The Porcupine Molecular Tagging System

Porcupine utilizes distinct, nanopore-orthogonal synthetic DNA strands termed molecular bits (molbits) to represent digital data on tagged surfaces.

Real-Time Raw Signal Classification

By classifying molbits directly from the raw electrical signal of a portable nanopore sequencer, the system achieves tag readout within seconds without requiring traditional basecalling.

Environmental Robustness and Shelf Life

Dehydrating assembled molbits provides environmental stability and contamination resistance, establishing a durable, low-cost molecular barcode architecture.

talks.title: Digital Health Tech in NIH All of Us
talks.teaser: Explores digital health data collection and privacy considerations within the NIH All of Us Research Program.
talks.summary:
The NIH All of Us Research Program

The National Institutes of Health initiative aims to enroll over one million diverse participants to collect electronic health records, genomic data, and physical measurements for precision medicine research.

Integrating Bring Your Own Device Health Data

A dedicated BYOD pilot enables participants to donate longitudinal digital health data from consumer wearables like Fitbit and Apple HealthKit devices into the secure research workbench.

Evaluating Population Diversity and Representation

Assessing participant representation among wearable donors compared to the broader population ensures researchers address demographic disparities in biomedical datasets.

Future Directions in Digital Health Technologies

Upcoming research protocols plan to expand wearable sensor integration while maintaining strict data governance, cryptographic protections, and participant privacy.

talks.title: Russian Cyber Threats in Pandemic Era
talks.teaser: Surveys Russian state-sponsored cyber operations targeting universities, hospitals, and medical research facilities during the pandemic.
talks.summary:
Targeting Healthcare and Research Facilities

State-sponsored adversaries exploited the COVID-19 pandemic to target Western hospitals, academic institutions, and vaccine research centers to exfiltrate proprietary scientific data.

Tactics of Russian Advanced Persistent Threats

The presentation analyzes the TTPs of state-aligned APT groups, reviewing spearphishing entry vectors, third-party supply chain compromises, and dark web coordination.

The Role of Intelligence Agencies and Criminal Proxies

Structural units within the FSB and GRU increasingly outsource cyber operations to criminal ransomware networks, blurring the line between financial extortion and state-directed espionage.

Strategic Defense and Technological Trends

Countering sophisticated state-sponsored operations requires continuous threat intelligence sharing, supply chain auditing, and hardening critical medical research infrastructure.

talks.title: Hacking the Insulin Supply Chain
talks.teaser: Examines the Open Insulin project's community protocols and open-source hardware designed to produce accessible, low-cost insulin.
talks.summary:
The Global Insulin Access Crisis

Despite insulin being developed a century ago, astronomical costs and pharmaceutical market concentration leave nearly half of insulin-dependent patients worldwide without reliable access.

The Open Insulin Project Mission

A global collective of volunteer biohackers and community laboratories is engineering open-source protocols, cell lines, and purification hardware to produce affordable off-patent insulin.

Open Hardware and Biomanufacturing Protocols

By developing transparent biomanufacturing equipment, the project aims to decentralize drug synthesis and enable regional micro-production facilities.

Patient-Led Biomedical Research

The initiative demonstrates how grassroots open-source collaboration can disrupt entrenched medical supply chains and democratize essential pharmaceutical manufacturing.

talks.title: Redefining Patient Safety
talks.teaser: Advocates expanding traditional patient safety definitions to incorporate cybersecurity risks, digital footprints, and data rights.
talks.summary:
The Digital Transformation of Clinical Care

Digital health tools, remote patient monitoring devices, and connected home sensors promise enhanced care accessibility but introduce unprecedented risk profiles.

Limitations of Traditional Risk-Benefit Analyses

Conventional clinical risk assessments evaluate biological efficacy and physical toxicity, often ignoring cybersecurity vulnerabilities and third-party data tracking.

Quantifying Harm from Digital Health Footprints

Insecure digital health platforms expose patients to targeted discrimination, loss of insurance coverage, and direct clinical disruption through compromised device communications.

Integrating Cybersecurity into Patient Safety Standards

Health systems and regulatory bodies must modernize clinical governance by embedding data rights and cybersecurity baselines directly into the core definition of patient safety.

talks.title: Cybersecurity Informed Consent for Medical Devices
talks.teaser: Presents a clinical framework for cybersecurity informed consent to communicate device vulnerability risks to patients.
talks.summary:
The Medical Device Cybersecurity Awareness Gap

Patients and clinicians frequently lack awareness of the network vulnerabilities, update lifecycles, and remote tampering risks inherent to implanted and connected medical devices.

The Cybersecurity Informed Consent Framework

A multidisciplinary team of clinicians, ethical hackers, and bioethicists formulated a structured framework to transparently disclose cybersecurity risks during clinical consent procedures.

Advisory Collaboration and Scenario Modeling

A thirty-person advisory board modeled real-world clinical scenarios, evaluating legal precedents and regulatory requirements to craft accessible consent disclosures.

Clinical Implementation and Assessment

The project transitions to clinical pilot testing to evaluate whether standardized cybersecurity disclosures improve patient trust without deterring adoption of life-saving therapies.

talks.title: Institutional Review Board for Biohackers
talks.teaser: Examines ethical review standards and institutional review boards adapted for independent biohackers and community labs.
talks.summary:
In this governance session from the DEF CON Safe Mode Biohacking Village, Sarah Blossom Ware, founder of the BioBlaze community wet lab in Chicago, addresses the necessity of Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) for independent scientific research. Opening at 00:00, Sarah outlines the growing community of citizen scientists operating outside traditional academia.

At 03:02, she defines the modern biohacker demographic, highlighting researchers pursuing independent biological experimentation in community labs and independent spaces. At 06:02, the talk examines the ethical mandate of IRBs in evaluating research protocols, protecting human subjects, and ensuring informed consent.

Concluding at 09:02 and 12:00, Sarah presents a framework for decentralized, community-driven IRBs, explaining how peer ethical review builds public trust, qualifies biohackers for institutional funding, and facilitates collaboration with established public health authorities. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Medical Tech: How Do We Unfuck Things
talks.teaser: Explores pragmatic strategies for securing medical technologies, improving device forensics, and remediating clinical vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
Forensics and cybersecurity researcher Veronica Schmitt examines the critical vulnerabilities and operational complexities of modern healthcare technology in the Biohacking Village [00:00, 05:17].

Schmitt examines the systemic hurdles in medical technology security, analyzing proprietary vendor lock-in that restricts hospital biomedical teams from independently servicing or patching vulnerable clinical hardware [10:33]. She contrasts the stringent operational requirements of hospital clinical environments with traditional enterprise IT [16:04], investigating insider threat dynamics, black-market sales of electronic health records [21:53], and regulatory oversight by the FDA, while proposing collaborative strategies for clinical cybersecurity resilience.

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: What's Up with Proposed Privacy Legislation
talks.teaser: Breaks down proposed federal and state privacy legislation impacting consumer health data and digital therapeutics.
talks.summary:
Social Engineering and Human-Oriented Security

This presentation explores social engineering attacks and human vulnerability in security systems. Topics include psychological manipulation, pretexting, credential harvesting, and how attackers exploit human nature to bypass technical defenses.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: MedICS
talks.teaser: Analyzes industrial control and embedded medical device architectures within hospital clinical networks.
talks.summary:
This talk covers industrial control systems security and critical infrastructure protection.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: Advancing Medical Device Security
talks.teaser: Convenes health system leaders and security professionals to discuss advancing cybersecurity across medical device ecosystems.
talks.summary:
In this healthcare cybersecurity briefing from the DEF CON Safe Mode Biohacking Village, Mitch Parker, Information Security Officer at IU Health, discusses strategies for advancing medical device security through industry-wide collaboration. Opening at 00:00, Mitch explores the unique clinical and technological challenges of safeguarding patient-connected devices.

At 13:01, the presentation examines budget and operational constraints in healthcare delivery organizations, emphasizing cost-effective security solutions that protect clinical networks without disrupting patient care. At 26:00, Mitch highlights cross-sector advocacy initiatives, detailing how the Health Sector Coordinating Council (HSCC) and H-ISAC engaged major operating system vendors to secure extended security patches for legacy clinical equipment.

Concluding at 39:00, Mitch evaluates network micro-segmentation architectures and urges continuous collaboration between clinical engineers, device manufacturers, and security researchers to protect healthcare infrastructure. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Diabetes Panel
talks.teaser: Explores patient-led innovation, closed-loop artificial pancreas systems, and cybersecurity challenges in diabetes management.
talks.summary:
Dina Truxius of the German Federal Office for Information Security (BSI), Julian Suleder of ERNW Research, and Michael Shannon of Harbor Labs convene for an expert panel on insulin pump cybersecurity and DIY diabetes ecosystems in the Biohacking Village [00:00, 00:11].

The panelists explore the rise of patient-led DIY artificial pancreas systems (#WeAreNotWaiting), analyzing how open-source algorithms interface with commercial continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) and infusion pumps to automate insulin delivery [01:14]. They establish a formal threat model covering mobile control apps, smartphone operating systems, and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) communication channels [09:24, 18:02]. The discussion highlights mutual authentication weaknesses and spoofing risks in wireless pump protocols [26:20], balancing the clinical necessity of patient-driven innovation against the vital imperative of medical device safety and coordinated vulnerability disclosure [35:07].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Understanding DIYBio and Community Labs
talks.teaser: Examines the culture, safety practices, and governance models of do-it-yourself biology and community research laboratories.
talks.summary:
DEF CON Security Research Presentation

This talk covers technical security topics and vulnerability research. The presentation includes discussion of contemporary security challenges, demonstrations of exploitation techniques, and insights into defensive countermeasures and security best practices.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: How to Grow a Brain in a Jar
talks.teaser: Demonstrates techniques for culturing biological neural networks and interfacing biological neurons with computational hardware.
talks.summary:
This talk explores artificial intelligence and machine learning security challenges.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: The Underestimated Threat Vector: Homogeneity
talks.teaser: Analyzes systemic risks posed by software and hardware homogeneity across hospital medical device fleets.
talks.summary:
In this reflective presentation from the DEF CON Safe Mode Biohacking Village, the speaker analyzes cognitive homogeneity as an underestimated vulnerability in cybersecurity threat modeling. Opening at 00:00, the talk connects broader societal discussions on diversity directly to operational security efficacy.

At 03:01, the presenter examines structural barriers that prevent non-traditional talent from entering cybersecurity, advocating for accessible mentorship and hiring pathways. At 06:02, the speaker details the core thesis: when security teams share identical backgrounds and thinking patterns, they create collective blind spots that adversaries actively exploit.

Concluding at 09:01, the presentation argues that securing the future of connected healthcare, biological data, and complex cyber-physical systems demands diverse, multidisciplinary perspectives to challenge assumptions and identify hidden attack vectors. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Open Ventilator Remote Monitoring Project
talks.teaser: Presents an open-source hardware and software telemetry platform designed to monitor emergency hospital ventilators remotely.
talks.summary:
Sam Cervantes and Dave present the Open Ventilator Remote Monitoring Project in the Biohacking Village, an open-source engineering initiative developed to enable remote monitoring of hospital mechanical ventilators during the COVID-19 pandemic [00:00, 00:04].

The speakers describe how remote telemetry protected clinical staff and conserved personal protective equipment (PPE) by allowing intensive care personnel to monitor vital ventilator parameters from outside isolated patient rooms [05:44]. They discuss the technical hurdles of interfacing telemetry software with diverse open-source hardware designs—including MIT and Arduino-based ventilator controllers [11:51]—while detailing code reviews, automated data sanitization routines, and encryption protocols implemented to ensure clinical reliability and protect patient privacy [18:22, 25:01].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.summary:
Social Engineering and Human-Oriented Security

talks.title: Infodemic: Threat Models
talks.teaser: Applies cybersecurity threat modeling to health misinformation, medical disinformation campaigns, and patient vulnerability.
talks.summary:
In this public health security presentation from the DEF CON Safe Mode Biohacking Village, researcher Andrea delivers an analysis of threat models targeting patient communities across social networks. Opening at 00:00, Andrea introduces the concept of an "infodemic"—the rapid, uncontrolled spread of misinformation during health crises.

At 04:02, the talk explores how organized disinformation campaigns exploit social platform algorithms to amplify unverified medical treatments and promote medical fraud. At 08:01, Andrea presents sobering real-world case studies demonstrating how online medical misinformation has resulted in tragic patient harm and preventable deaths.

Concluding at 12:00 and 16:01, the speaker emphasizes the lack of safe digital spaces for vulnerable patients to discuss health conditions and outlines defensive threat models to identify, track, and counter adversarial medical disinformation. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Chinese Military Lab Mission + COVID-19
talks.teaser: Examines military research facilities and biosecurity threat capabilities in the People's Republic of China.
talks.summary:
Military Biological Facilities and Research Missions

The presentation surveys military research laboratories in the People's Republic of China and their operational focus within national defense and biotechnology programs.

Evaluating Biosecurity and Dual-Use Research Risks

Assessing dual-use scientific research requires analyzing pathogen containment protocols, defense funding, and the potential implications of viral modification programs.

Strategic Geopolitical Implications

Understanding military biological programs provides critical context for global biosecurity threat intelligence, disease surveillance, and international monitoring frameworks.

talks.title: How COVID19 Changed Cyber Disaster Medicine
talks.teaser: Physician-hackers Christian Dameff and Jeff Tully share lessons from treating COVID-19 patients to reframe clinical cyber disaster preparedness.
talks.summary:
Cybersecurity as Clinical Patient Safety

Vulnerabilities in healthcare infrastructure extend far beyond patient data breaches, directly impacting clinical care continuity and clinical patient outcomes during emergencies.

Parallels Between Pandemics and Cyber Disasters

Practicing physicians on the COVID-19 frontlines compare hospital crisis response to cyber disaster medicine, highlighting how systemic strain exposes single points of failure.

Reframing Healthcare Cyber Resilience

Experiences managing clinical surge capacity offer actionable lessons for designing resilient clinical workflows that withstand sustained ransomware disruptions and operational downtime.

talks.title: INCLUDES NO DIRT: Threat Modeling
talks.teaser: Introduces the INCLUDES NO DIRT threat modeling methodology developed at Omada Health to integrate privacy, security, and compliance.
talks.summary:
Bridging Security, Privacy, and Compliance

Organizations face numerous regulatory mandates for risk assessments, yet often lack consistent, scalable methodologies that bridge the gap between technical security and data privacy.

The INCLUDES NO DIRT Threat Modeling Framework

Omada Health designed the INCLUDES NO DIRT process to synthesize disparate risk models across healthcare delivery, incorporating clinical device interactions and digital coaching.

Practical Application to Connected Health

Demonstrating the methodology against real-world connected medical devices and digital coaching workflows illustrates how cross-disciplinary threat modeling improves risk mitigation efficiency.

talks.title: Open Ventilator Remote Monitoring Project
talks.teaser: Details the development, acoustic alarm monitoring features, and clinical lab testing of the Open Ventilator Remote Monitoring Project.
talks.summary:
Rapid Prototyping for Critical Care Equipment

In response to projected ventilator shortages during the early stages of the pandemic, open-source engineers collaborated with Massachusetts healthcare networks to build rapid prototype ventilators.

Centralized Alarm and Telemetry Aggregation

The Open Ventilator Monitoring Project developed a centralized telemetry bridge that ingests alarms and vital data from disparate ventilators into a unified dashboard at the nursing station.

Acoustic Monitoring of Ventilator Alarms

To address closed-door infection isolation protocols, the system integrated external audio acoustic sensors to detect and alert staff to high-priority ventilator alarm frequencies.

Extensibility and Lessons for Emergency Engineering

Although traditional ventilator shortages were averted, the project demonstrated an extensible API and plugin architecture for deploying emergency open-source medical software under crisis conditions.

talks.title: Biohacking Village Keynote: Healthcare Voices
talks.teaser: Biohacking Village Executive Director Nina Alli interviews clinical professionals, patients, and hackers on the future of healthcare security.
talks.summary:
Unfiltered Perspectives on Healthcare Security

Biohacking Village Executive Director Nina Alli interviews a diverse group of clinical practitioners, cybersecurity researchers, and patients to capture unscripted reactions on modern healthcare.

Connecting Clinical Practice with Security Research

Interviewees from digital forensics, telemedicine, data science, and patient advocacy explore systemic vulnerabilities and call for actionable reform across the biomedical industry.

Fostering Community Action in Biohacking

The discussion highlights the vital role of grassroots security communities in bridging the gap between hospital administrators, medical device manufacturers, and independent researchers.

talks.title: How Independent Researchers Work with MDMs
talks.teaser: Security researchers and medical device manufacturers share insights on coordinated vulnerability disclosure and addressing legacy devices.
talks.summary:
Navigating the Researcher-Manufacturer Relationship

Leading security researchers share experiences collaborating with Medical Device Manufacturers (MDMs), discussing historical points of friction and emerging partnerships.

Maturing Product Security Programs

Embracing external vulnerability reports and maintaining open dialogue with independent researchers enables medical device manufacturers to transition from reactive patching to proactive security postures.

Tackling Legacy Medical Devices

The panel explores technical and regulatory strategies for addressing legacy devices in clinical use that lack native update mechanisms or long-term vendor support.

talks.title: Why Is Security Hard?
talks.teaser: Seth Carmody examines the structural, economic, and regulatory obstacles to achieving effective cybersecurity across the medical device ecosystem.
talks.summary:
Understanding Inherent Complexities in Healthcare

Former FDA cybersecurity strategist Seth Carmody explores why securing healthcare environments and medical technology remains notoriously challenging compared to other sectors.

Regulatory Frameworks and Market Incentives

The presentation examines how economic constraints, legacy clinical infrastructure, and lengthy regulatory approval cycles create unique hurdles for vulnerability remediation.

Pragmatic Approaches to Product Security

Carmody outlines realistic paths forward for manufacturers and healthcare delivery organizations to align safety, usability, and proactive security engineering.

talks.title: Vulnerability Disclosure Panel: Healing the Healthcare Immune System
talks.teaser: Chloe Messdaghi, Eric, and Bugcrowd founder Casey Ellis discuss the legal perils and necessity of coordinated vulnerability disclosure in healthcare, introducing the disclose.io project.
talks.summary:
The Legal Chill Over Medical Vulnerability Research

Despite good faith efforts by security researchers to discover flaws in healthcare technology, legacy legal statutes like the CFAA and DMCA Section 1201 create severe chilling effects.

The Reality of Hospital Asset and Vulnerability Management

Panelists examine operational vulnerabilities within healthcare networks, from absent device inventories to unpatched clinical systems where uptime and patient availability supersede security maintenance.

Standardizing Vulnerability Disclosure with disclose.io

Casey Ellis outlines the evolution of disclose.io, an open-source initiative providing standardized, legally protective vulnerability disclosure program (VDP) terms and safe harbor language.

Fostering an Internet Immune System for Healthcare

The panel outlines practical steps for hospitals, medical device manufacturers, and security researchers to establish trust, streamline triage, and protect clinical patient safety.
